# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
Hypothesis title: Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin Nup98 after cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing causes selective nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS

This proposal applies to neuronal models of TDP-43 proteinopathy used for sporadic ALS and TDP-43-positive ALS/FTD. C9orf72-repeat disease is kept as a separate context.

Supported premises. Insoluble TDP-43 aggregates associate with nuclear-pore and transport components. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and nucleocytoplasmic transport in experimental cells, and related pore pathology occurs in ALS tissue [S1]. This links TDP-43 pathology with transport disruption, while nucleoporin phosphorylation remains unestablished. Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies can form independently of conventional stress granules, mislocalize transport-associated proteins, and accompany impaired nuclear import, loss of nuclear TDP-43, and cell death [S3]. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulates in these assemblies; the modified protein is TDP-43, a different event from nucleoporin phosphorylation [S3]. Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA is linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons [S2]. Cellular stress recruits transport factors into stress granules and impairs nucleocytoplasmic transport, and altering stress-granule assembly modifies transport defects and disease-model phenotypes [S4]. Beside [S3], the stress-granule route is sufficient in some models and dispensable in others.

Initiating mechanism and downstream response. The initiating mechanism is stress-granule-independent cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing [S3]. Phosphorylation of the FG-nucleoporin Nup98 is the proposed proximal pore modification that causes selective nuclear-import failure. Loss of nuclear TDP-43, further cytoplasmic accumulation, and neuronal death are downstream responses to the import block. Any later feedback from nuclear TDP-43 loss stays downstream of Nup98 phosphorylation.

Speculative bridges. The packet names no nucleoporin kinase, site, or biophysical effect, so the following links are assumptions. First, cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies activate a stress-responsive proline-directed kinase that phosphorylates Nup98 within or adjacent to its FG-repeat region. Listing ERK1/2 or CDK5 as candidates is unverified prior knowledge from other cellular settings, outside [S1]–[S4]. Second, phosphorylation weakens FG-repeat cohesion or karyopherin–FG binding and slows facilitated import while the pore scaffold remains largely assembled. Third, this intrinsic change converts TDP-43 demixing into import failure beyond coexisting sequestration of transport factors. Sites will be mapped by phosphoproteomics in the same neurons; designating a residue beforehand would be a further unsupported assumption. Choosing Nup98 rather than another FG-nucleoporin is unverified prior knowledge.

Alternative explanations. One alternative is sequestration of nuclear-transport factors inside stress granules, a route that impairs transport in [S4]. A second is recruitment of those factors into stress-granule-independent TDP-43 assemblies [S3], followed by nucleoporin mislocalization of the kind reported in [S1]. A third is import failure as a byproduct of broad proteotoxic stress, with Nup98 phosphorylation only correlated. In C9orf72 models, RanGAP mislocalization can account for import failure [S2], and the present hypothesis limits that account to the C9orf72 context.

Discriminating preclinical test. Use rodent spinal motor neurons and human iPSC-derived motor neurons with inducible cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies matched to [S3], plus a matched arm in which stress-granule nucleation is prevented. Include C9orf72-repeat neurons only as a boundary culture. At short intervals, quantify Nup98 phosphorylation by phosphoproteomics, FG-nucleoporin localization, an NLS import reporter, the nuclear-to-cytoplasmic TDP-43 ratio, G3BP1-positive stress granules, and a cell-death marker. After mapping sites, replace endogenous Nup98 with a phospho-null sequence or a phosphomimetic sequence. The hypothesis predicts that phospho-null Nup98 preserves NLS import and nuclear TDP-43 despite cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies, whether or not stress granules form, and that phosphomimetic Nup98 impairs import in neurons lacking both TDP-43 assemblies and stress granules. Stress-granule blockade, a perturbation class that modifies phenotypes in [S4], is predicted to leave Nup98 phosphorylation and the import defect in place. Import preserved by phospho-null Nup98 while transport factors remain co-localized with cytoplasmic TDP-43 would favor a pore-intrinsic cause over sequestration alone. Nup98 site occupancy is predicted to rise before the NLS reporter slows and before nuclear TDP-43 falls.

Falsifying observation. The hypothesis is falsified if Nup98 phosphosite occupancy stays flat until after the import defect, if phospho-null Nup98 leaves import failure, nuclear TDP-43 loss, and cell death unchanged, or if phosphomimetic Nup98 leaves import intact when stress-granule sequestration is absent. Recovery of import after stress-granule disruption, while Nup98 phosphorylation persists, also falsifies a necessary role for that phosphorylation.

Limitations. The kinase, the sites, the stoichiometry, and the focus on Nup98 are assumptions, and any mitotic analogy for Nup98 is unverified prior knowledge. Phosphorylation of other nucleoporins could bypass a Nup98 phospho-null allele. A phosphomimetic protein can exceed the modification level of chronic human tissue. Support in this TDP-43 model would leave the C9orf72 route [S2] and other sporadic trajectories [S1] unresolved. The design tests causality and stops short of a therapeutic claim.

Ranked proposal:
Phosphorylation of FG-nucleoporin Nup98 after cytoplasmic TDP-43 demixing causes selective nuclear-import failure in TDP-43 proteinopathy models of ALS
